tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create all three):
  skills/podcast-show-notes/SKILL.md
  docs/RUNBOOK-show-notes-and-publication.md
  tests/test_docs_match_code.py

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — read these files first and document what they ACTUALLY do. Do not invent behaviour; every claim in your docs must be checkable against the code:
  server/pipeline/show_notes_structure.py   (SECTIONS, REQUIRED_SECTIONS, build_show_notes,
                                             render_markdown, validate_show_notes, MIN_QUOTES,
                                             MIN_HIGHLIGHTS)
  server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py    (gather_guest_email_context, download_headshot,
                                             MAX_HEADSHOT_BYTES)
  server/pipeline/content_mechanics.py      (check_mechanics, split_run_on, revision_prompt,
                                             MAX_SENTENCE_WORDS)
  server/pipeline/publish_preflight.py      (evaluate_episode and its 12 checks)
  server/pipeline/outbound.py               (dispatch: the mandatory gateway, its 10 ordered
                                             steps, kill switch, loop_mode/live + human ack)
  server/config.py                          (HUBSPOT_MEETING_LINK, PODCAST_SHOW_URL,
                                             HUBSPOT_BCC)

WRITE skills/podcast-show-notes/SKILL.md — an operator-facing skill for producing show notes:
  * Front matter with a name and a one-line description, matching the style of the other
    skills already in skills/ (read one first).
  * The canonical section order and which sections are REQUIRED, taken from the code
    constants, not from memory.
  * Source-of-truth rules: guest bio and links come from the GUEST'S OWN email messages
    (gather_guest_email_context strips quoted-reply blocks so the host's words are never
    mined as guest bio); the headshot comes from an image attachment in that thread,
    verified by magic number; quotes come from the recording transcript and MUST carry a
    speaker and a timestamp; the host's booking link is required on every episode.
  * A privacy rule stated plainly: a guest's email address is NEVER published unless the
    guest record sets share_email.
  * A short worked example using episode 104 (Dr. Fred H. Cho) showing the rendered shape.
  * A "what makes this fail" section listing the real defects this system was built after:
    a 42-word run-on that shipped in approved notes, an unattributed quote risk, and a
    missing booking link.

WRITE docs/RUNBOOK-show-notes-and-publication.md — the end-to-end operator runbook:
  * PART 1, show notes: gather guest email context -> download headshot -> pull quotes with
    timestamps -> build_show_notes -> validate_show_notes -> fix any violation (run-ons via
    content_mechanics.split_run_on) -> human review. State the exact function calls.
  * PART 2, publication: publish_preflight.evaluate_episode must be 12/12 BEFORE anything
    external; then per-channel human approval; then the outbound.dispatch gateway performs
    the send. Document that dispatch REFUSES unless loop_mode is live AND a human
    acknowledgement exists, that a shadow dispatch invokes the performer zero times, and
    that publish credentials live on the VPS, not the workstation.
  * A gates table: what blocks publication and how each clears.
  * A rollback/abort note: what to do if a send half-completes.
  * Do NOT claim any automation is live that is not. Where a step is manual today, say so.

WRITE tests/test_docs_match_code.py — tests that keep the docs HONEST (at least 4):
 (1) every section id in show_notes_structure.SECTIONS appears in SKILL.md, and every id
     named in SKILL.md exists in SECTIONS (both directions, so the doc cannot drift);
 (2) every function name the runbook instructs an operator to call actually exists and is
     importable from the module the runbook names;
 (3) NEGATIVE: the docs must NOT contain a hard-coded booking URL or show URL that differs
     from server.config.HUBSPOT_MEETING_LINK / PODCAST_SHOW_URL — assert any
     meetings.hubspot.com or buildingempires URL found in the docs equals the config value
     (this catches a stale link being copied into the doc);
 (4) NEGATIVE: the runbook must not claim external sending happens automatically — assert
     it contains the words describing human approval and does not contain a phrase asserting
     auto-send (choose a specific phrase set and document your choice in a comment);
 (5) REQUIRED_SECTIONS are all marked required in SKILL.md.
Tests must read the real files from the repo root, not fixtures.
tasks.verified: skill + runbook for show notes and publication, with tests that fail if the docs drift from the code or overclaim automation
